title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Price increase (4.5% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $10.32 sold near baseline (96, 104), vs baseline 96.6; no uplift observed. Price increase typically reduces demand.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note warns of short delivery. Supply risk reduces consumer demand. No prior data on this risk, so shrink effect.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.6. No events are scheduled, so no seasonal or holiday drivers. The price is 4.5% above regular, which historically correlates with a demand drop. Past weeks at $10.32 (same price) sold 96 and 104 units, near baseline—no lift. The supplier warning of short delivery suggests supply risk, reducing demand certainty. No past promotions at this price point. The uplift model suggests 1.00, but the price increase and supply risk warrant a downward adjustment. Evidence is thin (one price point, one supplier note), so shrink toward 1.0. Downside spread increases due to uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.8 - 233.4 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
